verdict.rationale: Consensus markets its literature-review feature as able to 'search, screen, extract, and synthesize' evidence. It documents per-paper PICO extraction, study-design classification, study-type filters and Deep Search across many studies, which together form a uniform per-paper extraction layer. But there is no documented systematic-review workflow where a researcher defines inclusion/exclusion criteria and applies them consistently across a paper set. Missing for 10: user-defined screening criteria applied consistently across papers, configurable extraction fields or tables, screening audit trail or decision logging, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can run a systematic screening and extraction workflow across many papers with consistent criteria

citations.quote: Search, screen, extract, and synthesize evidence faster—while keeping full transparency and scholarly rigor.
Extracted population, intervention, comparator, and outcome (PICO) where applicable
Filters allow narrowing by study type (RCT, meta-analysis, systematic review, observational), publication year, journal, open-access status, and discipline.
Deep Searches (more comprehensive Lit Reviews across many studies)
classifies each relevant paper as supporting, refuting, or mixed/inconclusive
